result.relation_rationale: The reported primary radiographic progression-free survival result exactly matches the requested outcome: time from randomisation to radiographic progression or death, measured using CT/MRI for soft-tissue progression and adapted PCWG2 criteria for bone progression. It compares the pooled randomized SOC-plus-abiraterone groups with the pooled randomized SOC-without-abiraterone groups in the overall intention-to-treat population, with the reported adjusted hazard ratio at the final planned analysis.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.
An endpoint label or definition does not prove objectivity, blinding, prespecification, or no alternative analyses.
A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.

consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive standard of care (n=296), standard of care plus radiotherapy

Randomisation and masking
Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
This randomisation process was performed via the
Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
until 2015, then by each investigator.
Randomisation was done using a minimisation
algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
A similar weight was given to each of the five
stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
treatment group. As the case report form gathered
information for patient stratification according to
high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
volume was defined as the presence of visceral
metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
masking was performed in this study.

62|Introduction
63|After several decades with no substantial progress, the
64|treatment of de novo (synchronous) metastatic prostate
65|cancer has drastically evolved in the past 10 years
66|with the addition of diverse treatments to androgen
67|deprivation therapy (ADT), the former standard of care
68|(SOC). The prognosis for men with de novo metastatic
69|castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) has been
70|improved by using ADT concomitantly with either
71|docetaxel1-5 or one of the second-generation androgen
72|receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone,6-8 apalutamide,9 or
73|enzalutamide10,11). In 2018, radiotherapy to the primary
74|tumour was also shown to extend the overall survival of
75|patients with low-volume metastatic burden.12 The
76|benefits of these various combinatory therapies were
77|confirmed by meta-analyses13-15 and have helped to shape
78|the current guidelines for the treatment of mCSPC.16-18
79|Nevertheless, it remains to be established whether
80|merging some of these new therapies could provide
81|further clinical benefits and, if so, what combination
82|might be most suitable for de novo mCSPC.19 Conducted
83|by a European consortium (PEACE),20 this study aimed to
84|evaluate the efficacy and safety of abiraterone plus
85|prednisone, with or without radiotherapy, in addition to
86|SOC (ADT with or without docetaxel).
87|Methods
88|Study design and participants
89|We conducted an open-label, randomised, active-
90|controlled, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design
91|(PEACE-1) at 77 sites across seven European countries
92|(Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and
93|Switzerland). The complete list of inclusion and exclusion
94|criteria is provided in the appendix (pp 5-6). Briefly, male
95|patients aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed
96|or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma
97|documented as de novo metastatic by bone scan, CT, or
98|MRI (according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid
99|Tumors [RECIST] version 1.1 criteria) and an Eastern
100|Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status
101|of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain) were eligible for inclusion,
102|provided they had received ADT for no more than
103|3 months before randomisation and had at least 6 weeks
104|between the initiation of ADT and the first docetaxel
105|dose. Patients with a pure small-cell carcinoma, or
106|previous prostate cancer treated by a definitive local
107|treatment were not eligible. All participants provided
108|written informed consent before any study-specific
109|procedures or randomisation were initiated.
110|The initial protocol was reviewed and first approved on
111|July 10, 2013, by the French Independent Ethics
112|Committee (Comité de Protection des Personnes Ile de
113|France VII). The protocol complied with the ethical
114|principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and was
115|approved by Institutional Review Boards at each study
116|site. The trial conformed with the International
117|Conference on Harmonization and Good Clinical
118|Practice guidelines, and applicable regulatory require
119|ments. Steering and Independent Data Monitoring
120|Committees roles and members are described in the
121|appendix (pp 3-4).
122|Two major protocol amendments were made during
123|the accrual period, to account for the evolution of SOC
124|for men with mCSPC. Although ADT alone was the SOC
125|when the trial began recruitment in 2013, the protocol
126|was amended on Oct 5, 2015 (273 patients had already
127|been accrued), to allow for docetaxel use in SOC
128|worldwide, after ADT with docetaxel had shown
129|improvement in overall survival.2,3 Then, in 2017, ADT
130|plus abiraterone was also shown to improve overall
131|Research in context
132|Evidence before this study
133|We searched PubMed from Jan 1, 1984, to Dec 31, 2012, for
134|papers in English, using the terms "prostate cancer",
135|"metastases", and "phase 3 trial", and found 16 studies. When
136|the PEACE-1 trial began in 2013, androgen deprivation
137|therapy (ADT) had for several decades been the standard of
138|care for men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate
139|cancer (mCSPC). All randomised trials conducted before the
140|mid-2010s had not shown improvement in outcomes with
141|new therapies compared with ADT. During recruitment for the
142|PEACE-1 trial (2013-18), overall survival of patients with de
143|novo mCSPC was shown to be improved by combining ADT
144|with either docetaxel or one of the second-generation
145|androgen receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone, apalutamide,
146|or enzalutamide) and radiotherapy to the primary tumour, in
147|men with low metastatic burden. It had not yet been shown
148|whether combining some of these new therapies with ADT in
149|triple therapy could provide further clinical benefits.
150|Added value of this study
151|To our knowledge, PEACE-1 is the first trial to show that
152|a triple systemic therapy-consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
153|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
154|(abiraterone, combined with prednisone)-improves both
155|radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival in
156|patients with de novo mCSPC, without excessively increasing
157|toxicity (mostly hypertension and aminotransferase increase).
158|Implications of all the available evidence
159|The findings from the PEACE-1 trial, combined with the evidence
160|from other studies, add weight to the concept that systemic
161|treatment intensification provides clinical benefit for men with
162|mCSPC and illustrate that early treatment intensification is more
163|effective than identical or similar treatments being used
164|sequentially when the disease has become castration-resistant.
165|At a minimum, patients with mCSPC with a high metastatic
166|burden who are fit enough to be treated with docetaxel should
167|be considered for this triple systemic therapy.

16|Randomisation and masking
17|Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the

19|radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
20|prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.

23|data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
24|facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
25|until 2015, then by each investigator.
26|Randomisation was done using a minimisation
27|algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
28|status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
29|hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
30|planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
31|disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
32|(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
33|without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
34|A similar weight was given to each of the five
35|stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
36|imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
37|treatment group. As the case report form gathered
38|information for patient stratification according to
39|high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
40|classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
41|volume was defined as the presence of visceral
42|metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
43|the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
44|was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
45|masking was performed in this study.
46|Procedures
47|In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
48|continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
49|releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
50|orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
51|of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
52|intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
53|dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
54|3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
55|stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
56|cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
57|on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
58|patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
59|had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
60|and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
61|assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
62|abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
63|prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
64|after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
65|before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
66|trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
67|for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
68|similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
69|resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
70|prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
71|administered until disease progression to castration
72|resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
73|or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
74|(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
75|were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
76|after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
77|after completion). Treatments given after disease
78|progression followed common practice, and investigators
79|were able to change therapy as they thought was most
80|appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
81|(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
82|even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment

85|duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
86|performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
87|detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
88|were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for

Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.

4|Discussion
5|To our knowledge, this is the first trial to show that a
6|triple systemic therapy, consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
7|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
8|(abiraterone), extends radiographic progression-free survival
9|and overall survival in patients with de novo mCSPC.
10|Whether the systemic treatment of high-volume disease
11|(ie, extended metastatic spread) should differ from that of
12|low-volume disease has been extensively debated. The
13|benefit of ADT with docetaxel has been clearly shown for
14|patients with mCSPC with high-volume disease,4,22 but
15|data collected from larger populations support a similar
16|benefit across high-volume and low-volume disease.3 This
17|discrepancy might result from different ratios of patients
18|with de novo versus relapsing low-volume disease being
19|included in these trials, because recurrences favour better
20|prognoses.23 Second-generation androgen receptor axis
21|inhibitors have shown overall survival benefits in patients
22|with mCSPC regardless of the disease volume
23|considered.5,9,10 In this trial, the mature data for men with
24|high-volume disease indicate a clear improvement in
25|both radiographic progression-free survival and overall
26|survival when abiraterone is added to ADT with docetaxel.
27|Even though the data on overall survival were immature
28|for patients with low-volume disease, an abiraterone-
29|mediated benefit in radiographic progression-free
30|survival was already apparent. Thus, ADT with docetaxel
31|plus abiraterone should be proposed as a new SOC for
32|patients presenting with high-volume disease who are fit
33|for docetaxel prescription. However, for patients with low-
34|volume disease, the decision of whether to use two or
35|three agents should be carefully considered by both the
36|patients and their oncologists, to determine whether a
37|major benefit in radiographic progression-free survival
38|(HR 0·58) is sufficient to justify a treatment inten
39|sification in a context of immature overall survival data. It
40|would also depend on whether an overall survival benefit
41|is required. Long-term data and consensus conferences
42|will allow for clinical practice guidance refinement.
43|As abiraterone can inhibit CYP3A4 in vitro,24 and as
44|CYP3A4 is involved in docetaxel elimination,25 the
45|concomitant administration of these two drugs could
46|potentially increase docetaxel exposure and thereby its
47|toxicity. However, no increase in chemotherapy-related
48|side-effects occurred in reaction to this concomitance,
49|which might suggest an absence of substantial drug-
50|drug interactions between abiraterone and docetaxel.
51|This finding is consistent with the observation that
52|abiraterone and docetaxel have similar pharmacokinetic
53|behaviour when administered alone or in combination.26
54|Similarly, abiraterone did not affect the clearance of
55|another taxane, cabazitaxel, by CYP3A.27 We also did not
56|observe an increase in haematological toxicity when
57|abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel, contrary to
58|a phase 2 trial in patients with mCRPC.28 The most

62|vs 13% of those who did not). This expected adverse event

Incidentally, the 19|ongoing phase 3 ARASENS (NCT02799602) and 20|ENZAMET (NCT02446405) trials are also testing the 21|combined efficacy of second-generation androgen 22|receptor axis inhibitors (darolutamide and enzalutamide, 23|respectively) with ADT and docetaxel, and their 24|upcoming overall survival results will put the benefits 25|of abiraterone in perspective. 26|Reaching treatment synergy and preventing acquired 27|resistance despite tumour clonal heterogeneity are 28|cardinal aspects of mCSPC management that require 29|an optimisation of the treatment framework. In 30|PEACE-1, significant survival benefits were obtained 31|when abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel. 32|Remarkably, these benefits were observed even though 33|more than 80% of the SOC without abiraterone group 34|eventually received a second-generation androgen 35|receptor axis inhibitor (mostly abiraterone or enzaluta 36|mide) to address cancer progression. Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.

consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive standard of care (n=296), standard of care plus radiotherapy
(n=293), standard of care plus abiraterone (n=292), or standard of care plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone (n=291).

Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.

consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive standard of care (n=296), standard of care plus radiotherapy
(n=293), standard of care plus abiraterone (n=292), or standard of care plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone (n=291).

77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate

77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
